title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
authors: J. Hoffmann, S. Borgeaud, A. Mensch, et al. (22 authors)
before: Scaling laws were read as licence to grow parameters faster than data.
problem: Everyone's models were far too large for the number of tokens they saw.
breakthrough: Over 400 training runs showing parameters and data should scale together, roughly 20 tokens per parameter. A 70B model beat the 280B Gopher.
why: It redirected the field from parameter count toward data, which is why capable small models exist at all.
next: Llama took it further, overtraining small models for cheap inference.
inherits: Compute allocation as a design decision, not an afterthought.
